question.leadin: This leader edited the Ems Dispatch, helping to start a war with France.
question.text: Name this man whose use of Realpolitik earned him the nickname the "Iron Chancellor."
question.clue: Count Vincent Benedetti delivered a message actually created by this man, and he had the May Laws implemented to supervise Catholic clergy as part of his Kulturkampf.

swap.leadin: Tsar Nicholas II and this man sent each other a series of ten telegrams in summer 1914 as their countries teetered on the brink of war.
swap.text: Nicholas II corresponded with this man, his cousin and the last Kaiser of Germany.
swap.clue: In an 1897 speech, this leader's foreign minister Bernhard von Bulow outlined how this ruler's nation wanted its "place in the sun."

question.leadin: During a failed coup d'etat, this man attempted to put Erich Ludendorff in power.
question.text: For 10 points, name this man, who, after his arrest for his leadership in that Beer Hall Putsch, composed Mein Kampf from his prison cell.
question.clue: Hans Ritter von Seisser and Otto von Lossow put down a rebellion led by this leader, and he consolidated power by executing Operation Hummingbird.

swap.text: The Weimar Republic was almost overthrown in this unsuccessful 1923 coup d'etat, which led to the imprisonment of Adolf Hitler.
swap.answer: Beer Hall Putsch or Munich Putsch
swap.clue: The fallout of this event saw the shutting down of the newspaper People's Observer.

question.text: Friedrich List was a proponent of this 19th century customs union; adopted by German states at the behest of Prussia, it freed up trade and migration along their borders while further excluding Austria.
question.clue: Karl Bruck advocated the entry of Austria, but this plan was halted by the minister of commerce, Delbruck.

swap.leadin: Neville Chamberlain claimed to have achieved "peace in our time" after appeasing the Germans at a conference in this city.
swap.text: Name this city that was the site of a failed 1923 coup d'etat (COO DAY-tar) that led to the arrest of Adolf Hitler.
swap.clue: That used in Rollerball is the BMW Headquarters and Museum.

question.leadin: Frederick II authorized this organization to expand to Kulm in the Golden Bull of Rimini.
question.text: Name this Germanic Crusader Order that lost the 1242 Battle of the Ice to the Kievan Rus under Alexander Nevsky.
question.answerHtml: Teutonic Knights [or the Teutonic Order; prompt on the Livonian Order with “what larger organization was it part of?”]
question.clue: The Golden Bull of Rimini confirmed some land holdings of this group, which absorbed the Livonian Order.

swap.leadin: This event was ostensibly a reaction to the murder of Ernst vom Rath.
swap.text: Name this November 1938 pogrom, in which the Nazi SA destroyed synagogues and Jewish businesses around Germany. Either the German or the English name is acceptable.
swap.clue: This event, coupled with a one-million-mark fine, was prompted by the murder by deranged teenager Herschel Grynzspan of Ernst vom Rath.

question.text: John George I ("the first"), the ruler of this state, was forced to ally with Gustavus Adolphus after his lands were invaded by Tilly shortly before Breitenfeld.
question.clue: During World War I, George V renamed a royal house named for this region, Coburg, and Gotha to the House of Windsor.

swap.text: Later, this Nazi was responsible for coordinating most of the train transit of Jews to death camps. He was executed by hanging in 1962.
swap.clue: He had posed as a chicken farmer named Otto Heninger and a clerk called Ricardo Clement between 1946 and 1960.

question.leadin: Answer the following about a school.
question.text: Established in 1919, this school of design moved to in 1926, and closed because of Nazi hostility in 1933.

swap.text: Due to his declining health, Luther could no longer defend his views, leaving this friend and colleague to assemble them into the 1530 Augsburg Confession.

question.leadin: The controversy over Gerald Ford's pardon of Nixon was exacerbated by media attention on his gaffes.
question.text: In an SNL sketch, Chevy Chase cemented Ford's clumsy persona by knocking over one of these plants that are decorated in the White House Blue Room and Rockefeller Center. Plantations in Oregon grow these holiday plants.
question.answerHtml: Christmas trees [accept evergreen trees; accept conifers; accept pine trees or Pinus; accept fir trees or Abies; accept spruce trees or Picea; prompt on trees]
question.clue: For two years in a row, the city of Rome installed one of these items nicknamed "Spelacchio" or "mangy."

swap.text: Barnstormers often performed in groups called Flying Circuses. This nobleman led a fighter pilot squadron in World War I nicknamed the Flying Circus.
swap.answerHtml: Manfred von Richthofen [or Manfred Albrecht Freiherr von Richthofen; or the Red Baron]
swap.clue: His 80 kills led all aces during war, though he did not survive it; his famed red Fokker triplane was downed in April 1918, with both Australian anti-aircraft gunners and Canadian pilot Roy Brown claiming credit.

question.leadin: Name these leaders of onetime Soviet bloc states.
question.text: This last East German leader replaced Erich Honecker in 1989 and watched helplessly as minor government official Gunter Schabowski accidentally opened the Berlin Wall.
question.clue: He succeeded Erich Honecker in a position he held for only three months in 1989, this last leader of the German Democratic Republic was sentenced to six and half years imprisonment for manslaughter in Berlin Wall-related deaths.

swap.leadin: After its failure at the Battle of Kursk, a tank destroyer named for this man was developed into the Elefant.
swap.text: Name this SS officer who also created a 188-ton, super-heavy tank ironically dubbed the Maus. This Bohemian-born man mainly worked out of a Stuttgart factory opened in 1931.

question.leadin: This man had little success in convincing the Catholic Church to act upon his namesake report.
question.text: Identify this man who helped deliver Zyklon B to concentration camps, but who also attempted to pass on details about the horrors of the Holocaust to men such as Goran von Otter. He's a character in William T. Vollmann's novel, Europe Central.
question.clue: This SS Officer assigned to the Hygiene Institute and charged with delivering Zyklon B wrote a report of what he witnessed in that time at camps like Belzec. He reportedly attempted to communicate the info to the Allies through a Swede named Goran van Otter.

swap.text: After the partition of Poland, Prussia created this puppet state centered around a western Polish city, through which Prussia controlled its section of the country.

question.leadin: A group of people from this polity were dumped in a squalid camp in Blackheath before being shipped off to work in naval stores in the Hudson Valley.
question.text: Daniel Defoe advocated for "poor" people from what polity during a 1700s refugee crisis? James I married off his daughter Elizabeth Stuart to a ruler of this polity who was made King of Bohemia in 1619.
question.answerHtml: the Palatinate [or Electoral Palatinate, Electorate of the Palatinate, Pfalz, Kurpfalz, or Rhineland-Palatinate; accept Poor Palatines or Elector Palatine]

swap.leadin: Identify the following about the Franco-Prussian War.
swap.text: Immediately following Mars-La-Tour, this engagement saw Prussian forces use Krupp breach-loading all-steel artillery, and saw von Moltke trap Bazaine in the city of Metz, where a siege followed this battle.
